questions.question_text: A medicine is prescribed to relieve pain without treating the infection causing it. Which broad class best describes its immediate purpose?
questions.explanation: Analgesics reduce pain; they do not necessarily remove its cause.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why should an antibiotic course generally be taken as prescribed rather than stopped as soon as symptoms improve?
questions.option_a: Stopping it immediately makes viruses reproduce
questions.option_b: Surviving bacteria may multiply and contribute to drug resistance
questions.option_d: The medicine would turn into an antacid
questions.explanation: Incomplete or inappropriate antibiotic use can leave less-susceptible bacteria behind; antibiotics do not treat viral infections.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which use correctly distinguishes an antiseptic from a disinfectant?
questions.option_a: An antiseptic is used only to preserve food
questions.option_b: The two terms mean sweetening agents
questions.option_c: An antiseptic is suitable for living tissue; a disinfectant is used on non-living surfaces
questions.option_d: A disinfectant is always safe to swallow
questions.explanation: Antiseptics are formulated for application to living tissue; disinfectants are generally used on objects and surfaces.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient with a bacterial disease is given a vaccine after symptoms have already begun. What is the main reason this is not a substitute for an indicated treatment?
questions.option_a: Vaccines digest bacterial cell walls in the stomach
questions.option_c: Vaccines work only by lowering body temperature
questions.option_d: Vaccination primarily prepares immune memory and is preventive
questions.explanation: Vaccines stimulate an immune response that can protect against future infection; they are not a general immediate cure.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which food-storage practice most directly slows oxidative rancidity in a packet of fried snacks?
questions.option_a: Removing much of the air and limiting exposure to light
questions.option_b: Keeping the packet open in warm sunlight
questions.option_d: Storing it beside a source of heat
questions.explanation: Oxygen, light and heat can accelerate oxidation of fats; suitable packaging and cool storage slow it.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is nitrogen sometimes flushed into packages of foods rich in oils?
questions.option_a: It makes the food strongly acidic
questions.option_b: It displaces oxygen and reduces oxidation
questions.option_d: It converts oil directly into protein
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is relatively unreactive and can reduce contact between the food and oxygen.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A label lists sodium benzoate in a packaged acidic beverage. What is its intended role?
questions.explanation: Sodium benzoate is used as a preservative in suitable acidic foods and beverages.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement best describes why an antioxidant may be added to an oil-containing food?
questions.option_a: It increases the food's water hardness
questions.option_b: It turns every fat into a carbohydrate
questions.option_d: It slows oxidation of susceptible food components
questions.explanation: Antioxidants retard oxidation and can delay rancidity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A household uses a chlorine-based chemical to disinfect a well after contamination. Which precaution is most important?
questions.option_a: Use only the recommended dose and allow the required contact time
questions.option_b: Add an arbitrary large amount to guarantee safety
questions.option_c: Mix it with every household cleaner
questions.option_d: Assume clear water needs no treatment
questions.explanation: Disinfection depends on dose and contact time; excess chlorine and incompatible mixtures can be hazardous.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement about oral rehydration solution (ORS) is most accurate?
questions.option_a: It works by removing all sodium from the blood
questions.option_b: Glucose and salts together support intestinal absorption of water
questions.option_c: It kills every pathogen in the intestine
questions.option_d: It replaces the need for all medical assessment
questions.explanation: Glucose-coupled sodium absorption helps water uptake; ORS replaces fluid and electrolytes but is not an antimicrobial drug.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A surface cleaner is labelled for floors, while a similarly named antiseptic is labelled for skin. Why should they not be interchanged?
questions.option_c: Their concentrations and formulations are intended for different exposure routes
questions.explanation: Products for surfaces may irritate or injure tissue; intended use and concentration matter.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly separates a medicine's therapeutic effect from its dosage form?
questions.option_a: A tablet is always an antibiotic
questions.option_c: A capsule identifies the medicine as a vaccine
questions.option_d: A tablet is a dosage form; an analgesic is a therapeutic class
questions.explanation: Dosage form describes how a medicine is delivered; therapeutic class describes its intended action.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why can a medicine approved for one person be unsafe for another without professional advice?
questions.option_a: Dose, allergies, age and other medicines can change its risks
questions.option_b: All medicines have identical effects in everyone
questions.option_c: Only the colour of a tablet changes its action
questions.option_d: Medicines cannot interact with one another
questions.explanation: Patient factors and drug interactions can affect safety and dosing.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which packaging choice is most directly useful for a medicine that degrades on exposure to moisture?
questions.option_a: A container with a loose lid
questions.explanation: A moisture barrier limits contact with water vapour and helps preserve a moisture-sensitive product.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A food label says 'use by' and the package has been opened and stored warm. Which conclusion is safest?
questions.option_b: Opening the pack sterilises its contents
questions.option_c: The printed date alone cannot guarantee safety after improper storage
questions.option_d: The food is safe indefinitely if it smells normal
questions.explanation: Storage conditions and handling affect safety; a date is not a substitute for safe storage or inspection.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which is the best reason not to use an antibiotic for an ordinary viral cold?
questions.option_a: Viruses are a type of mineral
questions.option_b: Antibiotics work only in cold weather
questions.option_c: A cold is always caused by a fungus
questions.option_d: Antibiotics target bacteria and do not act against viruses
questions.explanation: Antibacterial drugs do not treat viral infections; unnecessary use also promotes resistance.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A food preservative inhibits microbial growth. Which statement is still correct?
questions.option_a: Preservation does not make poor hygiene or unsafe storage acceptable
questions.option_b: It guarantees sterility under every condition
questions.option_d: It eliminates the need to follow the label
questions.explanation: Preservatives reduce spoilage under intended conditions but do not replace food-safety practices.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why are medicines generally kept in their original labelled containers?
questions.option_a: It prevents all possible side effects
questions.option_b: The label preserves identity, dose instructions and storage information
questions.option_c: The container makes every medicine safe at any dose
questions.option_d: The original colour activates the medicine
questions.explanation: Original labels help prevent mix-ups and provide essential instructions and warnings.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person takes an antihistamine and becomes drowsy. Which practical advice is most prudent until its effect is known?
questions.option_d: Take another dose to cancel drowsiness
questions.explanation: Some antihistamines can impair alertness; safety-sensitive activity should be avoided if drowsy.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT Science textbooks and exemplar problems, https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
